newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - DIRECT RESPONSE.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - DIRECT RESPONSE.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
Peter Wood, who revolutionised the UK insurance industry 11 years ago by circumventing insurance brokers and selling insurance direct to the public via the telephone, wants to do it all again.
Wood has left UK insurer Direct Line and is heading west to launch Direct Response - a bid to repeat the same experiment in the U.S.

Wood will invest $10 million in the company with friend and partner Jim Stone of the Plymouth Rock Insurance Company. It will operate initially in New York State, and Wood intends to use the red telephone which he has used so successfully as a marketing gimmick at Direct Line, and is considering using the jingle which goes with it.
In typical style Wood's plans are pretty aggressive. He wants to roll Direct Response out to more states on his way to what he claims will be $1 billion worth of premium income within 10 years.

This kind of talk is already being laughed of by some of America's existing domestic insurers. Indeed, at a property casualty insurance leadership forum in New York earlier this year, most of the chief executives present thought telephone selling was worth looking at but saw little potential for running an entire business from it. Buyers, they said, are too familiar with the traditional agent network, where you buy insurance from the guy you went to school with and who lives at the end of the block, to be attracted to dealing with a faceless person over the phone.

Doubtless Wood laughs back, for he heard exactly the same kind of arguments when he started Direct Line in the UK. He turned it into such a success that his bonus payments became an embarrassment to its owners, the Royal Bank of Scotland.

In 1993 the bank paid him 24 million to give up a scheme that had brought him 18.2 million that year. Since then, Direct Line's profits slumped from 112.2 million in 1995 to 26.5 million stg the following year as fierce competition in the motor insurance market lowered premiums. However, it has remained in the black while many of its rivals lost money.
The direct line concept has already been adapted by Spain's Bankinter, a partnership with the Royal Bank of Scotland, and Linea Directa is the fastest growing insurer.

The U.S. market will be more difficult to crack. Many U.S. insurers have some kind of telephone enquiry service advertised on direct mailshots, but have so far not explored the potential of direct selling.
Meanwhile Direct Response is busy hiring some fairly high-powered individuals and laying the groundwork for what is guaranteed to be, at the very least, an interesting experiment.
